name: xcospan-materials
description: Inspect and prepare local files for a task, preserving source references and selecting text, tables, or visual materials for analysis and reviewed cloud collaboration.
---

# Prepare local materials

Choose the files and representations needed for the user's goal. Reuse the host's available reading tools and domain Skills. Plain text and source code can be read directly; visual questions require inspecting the actual image or page. Spreadsheet calculations require a spreadsheet-capable tool that can inspect formulas, cell references, and calculated values.

## Extract document content

This Skill includes a local document extraction helper backed by Xberg. It detects formats from the file contents and filename. Query the installed engine's format registry when needed:

```sh
bun "<skill-directory>/extract.ts" --formats
bun "<skill-directory>/extract.ts" "<source-path>" --text-output "<new-material>.md" > "<extraction-output>.json"
```

Run these commands through the host shell tool, using its documented arguments. Code Mode executes tool-orchestration JavaScript in an isolated environment; use the shell tool to run Bun, Python, and installed file-processing programs.

The result contains the resolved `source`, a `sha256` fingerprint of the bytes processed, and the engine's `results`: content, tables, pages or sheets, metadata, and processing warnings. The optional `--text-output` writes the complete extracted content to a new UTF-8 Markdown file, preserving its line breaks. Read that file for the material, and inspect the JSON for source identity, structure, and warnings. Choose a fresh output path; existing files are preserved. Select the relevant portions while preserving headings, clause numbers, sheet names, units, and source references.

The helper supports document, presentation, spreadsheet, PDF, text, markup, email, and archive formats exposed by the installed engine. It processes a local byte snapshot. Extraction errors terminate the command. Processing warnings remain in the result and must be considered when judging coverage.

## Select the appropriate representation

- **Documents and presentations:** use extracted structure for textual analysis. Inspect the rendered original when layout, embedded objects, annotations, or visual relationships affect the task.
- **Spreadsheets:** extracted tables show stored values. Formula cells may have empty or stale cached values. Use a spreadsheet-capable tool to recalculate the workbook and verify exact cell-level provenance.
- **Scans and image text:** explicitly select local OCR and the material's languages. OCR uses the engine's native Tesseract backend; the selected language data must be available locally. Repeat the option for multilingual material:

  ```sh
  bun "<skill-directory>/extract.ts" "<source-path>" --ocr-language eng --ocr-language chi_sim --text-output "<new-material>.md" > "<extraction-output>.json"
  ```

- **Images and diagrams:** preserve the visual material when the task depends on it. OCR captures text; visual inspection establishes what the image shows. Use the available image redaction tool for image material selected for cloud collaboration. When the task requires a representation that the configured tools cannot prepare or review, report the missing capability before delegation.
- **Audio, video, or other specialized material:** use a local tool or Skill that supports the required transcription or analysis.

Keep the original file unchanged. Extraction output and metadata may contain private information. For cloud collaboration, select the necessary original text or images, complete each redaction review, then assemble the task for complete outbound approval. For prepared UTF-8 text, pass its path through `redact.files` together with the task handoff in `redact.content`. The plugin reads the full selected text through the host permission boundary; the model can reference the file without copying its contents into tool arguments. Choose a file containing the selected evidence when only part of a source is relevant. Source paths and extraction metadata stay local unless explicitly included in the reviewed task.

# opencode-XCoSpan > Local–cloud collaboration for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) — Per-request Routing, Local Redaction, Editable Review, Approved Cloud Tasks, and Live Progress. [![CI](https://github.com/XHToken/opencode-XCoSpan/actions/workflows/check.yml/badge.svg?branch=main&event=push)](https://github.com/XHToken/opencode-XCoSpan/actions/workflows/check.yml?query=branch%3Amain) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode-2.0.27-E8833A)](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins) [![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-%3E%3D22-43853D)](package.json) [![Bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bun-1.4.3-202124)](https://bun.sh/docs/installation) [![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-3178C6?logo=typescript&logoColor=white)](CONTRIBUTING.md) [![License: XHToken community](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-XHToken%20community-green)](https://github.com/XHToken/community/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Community](https://img.shields.io/badge/XHToken-Community-5865F2)](https://github.com/XHToken/community#contact) XCoSpan brings **local execution and reviewed cloud collaboration into one OpenCode session**. Choose your local and cloud models through `/xcospan`, then send tasks normally. Each new request is routed; the local model plans the work, uses tools and Skills, and prepares any cloud task for your review. Approved work returns to the local model for verification and delivery. [Installation](#installation) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Features](#features) · [Review and control](#review-and-control) · [Commands](#commands) · [Documentation](#documentation-and-contributing) ## Architecture

The local model selects the task's tools, context, and materials. XCoSpan connects routing, redaction, review, delegation, and result delivery through OpenCode's native sessions and interfaces. Cloud execution begins after approval of the complete outbound task. ## Features ### Routing and execution - **Per-request routing** — assess each new query using recent conversation context and available local capabilities. Choose local execution or cloud collaboration. - **Flexible local planning** — let the model select tools, Skills, relevant materials, and the sequence of actions required by the task. - **Independent model roles** — choose local and cloud models from OpenCode's provider catalog. Protocols, credentials, and model limits follow native provider configuration. ### Redaction and review - **Local material preparation** — extract relevant text and tables from documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, presentations, and other supported formats. - **Editable redaction review** — inspect the original and candidate after every redaction; edit and approve the content that may be used for collaboration. - **Complete outbound approval** — review the assembled task and materials before cloud execution. Approval is bound to the candidate revision. ### Progress and control - **Live execution visibility** — follow actual operations, targets, recent output, elapsed time, and available usage in the sidebar. - **Cancellation and recovery** — stop active work or recover delivery of a completed cloud result from persisted records. - **Native setup and lifecycle** — configure models, start, stop, disable, enable, and remove XCoSpan through `/xcospan`. ## Installation | Component | Requirement | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | | OpenCode | **2.0.27** | | Material extraction | **Bun 1.4.3** on the PATH used by OpenCode | ### npm package Install through OpenCode's plugin manager: ```sh opencode plugin add @iflytekopensource/opencode-xcospan ``` The command installs the plugin and adds it to your global OpenCode configuration. Reopen OpenCode after installation. Windows users can run the same command in PowerShell. Install Bun using the [official guide](https://bun.sh/docs/installation) to use the bundled material extraction helper. See [Compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) for operating systems, extraction binaries, OCR, and provider authentication. Development guidance is available in [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md). ### From source With Git and Bun 1.4.3 installed, run: ```sh git clone --depth 1 --branch main https://github.com/XHToken/opencode-XCoSpan.git cd opencode-XCoSpan bun install --frozen-lockfile bun run setup ``` Setup builds the plugin and registers the checkout in your global OpenCode configuration. Keep the checkout at this location and reopen OpenCode. See [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md#update-or-remove-a-source-checkout) for source updates and removal. ## Quick start After [installation](#installation), configure your models and send a task in OpenCode. ### 1. Open your workspace Reopen OpenCode after installation. From the directory where you want to work, run: ```sh opencode ``` ### 2. Choose models Enter `/xcospan` in the conversation and follow the interface: ```text Configure models → Choose the local model → Choose the cloud model → Test connection and tool calling → Save and start → Confirm model roles and choose the default for new sessions ``` | Setup action | Where to find it | | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Use an existing provider | Choose its model from the OpenCode catalog | | Connect an account | Select **Connect an account /connect**, then return to `/xcospan` | | Add your own endpoint | Select **Add a local or custom provider** | | Enable future sessions | Select **Use XCoSpan by default**, or open `/xcospan` → **Start** in a session | Both model roles require tool calling and may use the same model. Connection tests send requests to the selected providers and incur usage. ### 3. Send a task Once XCoSpan starts, send your task in the conversation. It routes the request, works locally, and prepares cloud collaboration when needed. Review each redaction and the complete outbound task when prompted, then follow progress and receive the result in the same session. > **Model endpoints:** a remote provider assigned to the local role receives original task inputs and local tool results. Choose endpoints according to your data requirements. See [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) and [Security](SECURITY.md).

## Review and control

### Two review stages | Stage | What you review | Available actions | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | | **Material review** | Original content and the redacted candidate, after every redaction | Compare, edit, approve, or cancel | | **Outbound review** | The complete task, related context, materials, and expected output | Edit, approve this revision, or cancel | Edits create a new revision; approval applies to that revision. Cancelling a review stops the current task, including concurrent pending reviews. Send a new request when you want to continue. ### Follow the work The sidebar reflects actual execution events: operations, targets, recent output, elapsed time, and available usage. Open `/xcospan-status` to inspect the same process in a narrow terminal. Missing usage or pricing is shown as unknown; routing and redaction usage is excluded from the displayed totals.
Keyboard shortcuts | Action | Shortcut | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------ | | Edit a candidate | Ctrl+E | | Move between fields | Tab / Shift+Tab | | Save edits | Ctrl+S | | Approve / cancel | Ctrl+A / Ctrl+X | | Switch comparison views | Ctrl+D | | Open the image viewer | Ctrl+O | | Pan / zoom / fit an image | Arrow keys / `=` and `-` / `0` |
## Commands | Command | Purpose | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- | | `/xcospan` | Configure models and manage the collaboration lifecycle | | `/xcospan-review` | Open pending material and outbound reviews | | `/xcospan-status` | Inspect progress, models, and usage | | `/xcospan-cancel` | Select and cancel a cloud task | | `/xcospan-recover` | Check and recover delivery of a completed result | Inside `/xcospan`: - **Stop the current task** interrupts the current session's work. - **Return to the previous agent** restores the previous agent and model. Sessions started directly in XCoSpan offer **Choose another agent**. - **Disable collaboration** stops related work and retains model configuration. **Enable collaboration** makes it available again. - **Remove plugin** removes the entry from the selected configuration source. Model accounts, conversation history, reviews, and user files remain available. Deleting an OpenCode conversation removes its associated XCoSpan reviews and run records. Deletions made while the plugin is unloaded are reconciled when it loads again. Check `/plugins` if another configuration source still loads XCoSpan. ## Working with materials The bundled **`xcospan-materials` Skill** guides task-driven selection and verification. The model chooses the relevant content and local tools for the task. | Material | Local preparation | | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Documents, PDFs, presentations, markup, and email | Extract relevant text and source references | | Spreadsheets and tables | Extract required tables; use local tools for calculations | | Scanned content | Run OCR with explicitly selected local Tesseract language data | | Images | Use suitable local tools for visual interpretation; image redaction requires a configured local service | The extraction helper uses [Xberg](https://github.com/xberg-io/xberg/tree/main/crates/xberg-node); `--formats` lists the installed engine's supported formats. Extraction preserves source references and warnings for inspection. See [Compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) for native dependencies and the [redaction service contract](docs/CONFIGURATION.md#redaction) for image support. ## Update or uninstall Check for updates and update the installed npm package: ```sh opencode plugin check @iflytekopensource/opencode-xcospan opencode plugin update @iflytekopensource/opencode-xcospan ``` Stop active work before updating, then reopen OpenCode. Use the exact configured package specifier if you installed a version or tag. To remove the plugin from global configuration: ```sh opencode plugin remove @iflytekopensource/opencode-xcospan ``` You can also open `/xcospan` → **Remove plugin** to select the configuration source. Confirm removal in `/plugins` and reopen OpenCode. Model accounts, conversations, and user files remain available. Source checkout updates and removal are described in [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md#update-or-remove-a-source-checkout). ## Documentation and contributing | Document | Contents | | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) | Model setup, routing, and redaction service contracts | | [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Execution flow, module responsibilities, and host integration | | [Compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) | Platforms, providers, protocols, and authentication | | [Testing](test/README.md) | Unit, native host, and real-model validation | | [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | User-visible changes and release history | | [Releasing](docs/RELEASING.md) | Package verification and release procedures | | [Security](SECURITY.md) | Data access, deployment boundaries, and vulnerability reporting | | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | Development setup, checks, and change guidelines | | [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) | Community standards and reporting | ### Development From a source checkout: ```sh bun install --frozen-lockfile bun run check bun run build ``` `check` runs type checks, formatting checks, and unit tests. Follow [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for native host validation and [Testing](test/README.md) for opt-in real-model tests. Report reproducible issues and propose focused changes on [GitHub](https://github.com/XHToken/opencode-XCoSpan/issues). ## Community XCoSpan is part of the [XHToken community](https://github.com/XHToken/community). Join the [community channels](https://github.com/XHToken/community#contact) for ecosystem discussions. Use this repository's [issues](https://github.com/XHToken/opencode-XCoSpan/issues) for bugs and feature requests, and follow [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) to submit changes. Contributors follow the [XHToken Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and sign the [Contributor License Agreement](https://github.com/XHToken/community/blob/main/CLA.md). ## License Licensed under the [XHToken community license](https://github.com/XHToken/community/blob/main/LICENSE) (Apache-2.0). See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for the full text and copyright notices. Package documentation, diagrams, and community guidance are included in the distribution.

# Testing

## Test layers

| Command                    | Scope                                                              | Requirements                                |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `bun run test`             | Unit tests                                                         | Bun, installed dependencies                 |
| `bun run test:integration` | Real OpenCode host and terminal with deterministic model responses | OpenCode 2.0.27 on PATH                     |
| `bun run test:package`     | Build, artifact checks, clean install, then host integration       | OpenCode, Bun, Node.js/npm                  |
| `bun run test:live`        | Real configured models, native TUI, synthetic materials            | Explicit live configuration and credentials |

Use `OPENCODE_BIN` to select the host executable. Integration tests isolate configuration, data and sessions in temporary directories; fixture providers run on loopback. Set `XCOSPAN_PUBLIC_WEB_TEST=1` to enable tests that contact public HTTP services.

The default `bun run test` runs only unit tests. Live tests incur provider usage and run only when explicitly invoked. CI runs unit tests and installed-package integration on Linux, macOS, and native Windows x64 with Node.js 22 and 24, without live credentials. Both npm and Bun installations exercise exports and native material extraction. Host/TUI integration runs against the npm-installed artifact. Workflow syntax is validated with actionlint and ShellCheck.

Use `bun run test:package --output dist/release` to retain a verified tarball and SHA-256 checksum. Use `--artifact /absolute/path/to/package.tgz` to test an existing artifact, including one downloaded from npm. See [Releasing](../docs/RELEASING.md) for workflow-based release validation.

## Live model configuration

Set `XCOSPAN_LIVE_CONFIG` to an untracked JSON file containing:

| Field        | Value                                            |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `localModel` | Native `{ providerID, id }` reference            |
| `cloudModel` | Native `{ providerID, id }` reference            |
| `providers`  | Native provider definitions keyed by provider ID |
| `websearch`  | Native OpenCode search configuration             |

Each selected provider must have an explicit HTTP(S) `settings.baseURL`, its native `package`, and an entry in `models` for the selected model. Use OpenCode's environment-variable credential references; provide those variables to the test process. Model capabilities, limits and request `body` overrides come from this file. Tests compare actual requests with the selected model and configured body fields.

The test host exposes the selected models under the isolated role names `local` and `cloud`. Its recording proxy forwards native request headers and JSON bodies to the configured base address. Use HTTP providers with JSON model requests; provider-specific transports and OAuth flows require separate validation.

```sh
XCOSPAN_LIVE_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/live-models.json bun run test:live
XCOSPAN_LIVE_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/live-models.json bun run test:live --test-name-pattern "real quick start"
XCOSPAN_LIVE_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/live-models.json bun run test:live --test-name-pattern "real sidebar"
```

In PowerShell, set the variable before running the same command:

```powershell
$env:XCOSPAN_LIVE_CONFIG = "C:\private\live-models.json"
bun run test:live --test-name-pattern "real quick start"
```

`XCOSPAN_PACKAGE` can point to an installed package directory to validate that artifact. Without it, live tests use the checkout. Configuration errors fail before starting the host.

Live artifacts are written to ignored `.local/live/`: request bodies, response streams, session records and terminal snapshots. They are diagnostic output and must be reviewed before sharing. Request records include start, first-byte, and last-observed-byte timestamps for latency analysis. Native session and run states establish execution completion. Request authorization headers are not recorded. Never use private documents in automated live tests.

The quick-start journey runs the same `opencode plugin add` command as the README against an isolated registry serving the real npm tarball. It preserves existing provider configuration, selects and probes model roles in the native TUI, then enters four consecutive tasks in one session: local calculation, reviewed text collaboration, reviewed file collaboration, and another local calculation. It edits outbound revisions and approves reviews through terminal input, records each phase, and checks actual cloud requests and sensitive-content isolation.

The registry fixture serves package metadata and the exact tarball bytes; dependencies come from npm. `XCOSPAN_TARBALL` selects an existing artifact, and `test:package` passes its verified artifact automatically. Native installation coverage includes repeat installation, configuration preservation, update checks, updates, and removal. This fixture validates native installation behavior; public registry availability and publish authentication require a real publication.

To test installation from npm, set `XCOSPAN_INSTALL_SPEC` to a published package version or dist-tag:

```sh
XCOSPAN_INSTALL_SPEC=@iflytekopensource/opencode-xcospan \
  XCOSPAN_LIVE_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/live-models.json \
  bun run test:live --test-name-pattern "real quick start"
```

This mode uses npm directly and fails if the requested package is unavailable. The Live models workflow exposes the same option as `install_spec`. Source registration is covered separately by the setup unit tests.

## Coverage

- Per-query routing, queued queries and return to local execution.
- Text/image review, editing, revision binding and complete outbound approval.
- Cloud context isolation and tool/network permissions.
- Streaming feedback, errors, retries and cancellation propagation.
- Restart recovery and single delivery.
- Model setup, lifecycle controls, concurrent edits and narrow/wide terminals.

Deterministic fixtures verify protocol and lifecycle behavior. Live tests additionally verify actual model interaction; analysis and redaction quality still require task-specific evaluation.

## Fixtures

`fixtures/materials/` contains synthetic document, spreadsheet, presentation, PDF, and scanned-image inputs. Unit tests execute the real extraction engine across these formats, plus text, HTML, CSV, JSON, RTF, and email. Regenerate the binary fixtures with:

```sh
uv run --with reportlab --with openpyxl --with python-docx --with python-pptx --with pillow test/fixtures/generate-materials.py
soffice --headless --convert-to doc --outdir test/fixtures/materials test/fixtures/materials/inspection.docx
```

The multi-file live test lets the model choose its local reading and calculation tools. The shipped extraction helper uses the installed Xberg native package. OCR tests need English Tesseract language data available to that engine. Exact workbook calculations need an appropriate local tool, such as Python with `openpyxl`. LibreOffice is used only to regenerate the legacy `.doc` test fixture.

`fixtures/boundary-probe/` tests extension permissions; `fixtures/delivery-barrier/` controls a crash point between completion and delivery. These are test-only plugins and are excluded from the published package.

The unchanged-candidate live test approves model-prepared material and outbound reviews without rewriting their fields. It checks that private fixture values stay out of the candidate and cloud requests, that collaboration completes, and that a subsequent local request stays local. Tests that edit candidates separately verify the review UI and approved-version contract.

The workflow matrix runs six consecutive requests in one session: local greeting, text collaboration, Markdown material collaboration, CSV material collaboration, a context-dependent follow-up, and local calculation. Run it with `bun run test:live --test-name-pattern "real workflow matrix"`. It checks review ordering, real cloud execution, delivery, local/cloud transitions, and sensitive-content isolation. It records routing decisions, tool calls, file-reference use, elapsed time, and model-quality observations in `workflow-matrix.json`.

This matrix simulates reviewer edits through the same RPC used by the TUI. If a synthetic fixture identifier remains in a redaction draft, the test explicitly edits that draft and records the edit before approval. The complete outbound candidate and actual cloud requests must satisfy the privacy checks. Arithmetic quality is recorded separately from workflow completion. The unchanged-candidate test retains its strict redaction-quality checks.

# Changelog

## 0.1.0 — 2026-10-26

### Community

- Adopt the XHToken community license (Apache-2.0) across the license text, package metadata, and documentation, retaining existing contributor attribution.
- Connect contribution guidance, conduct reporting, security reporting, and issue entry points to XHToken community policies.

### Collaboration

- Per-request local/cloud routing with configurable model roles and a strict `{ reason, route: 0 | 1 }` service contract.
- Capability-based routing and text redaction through English model instructions. Routing assesses local execution tools independently of cloud delegation.
- Text and optional image redaction review, editable outbound approval, and version-bound delegation.
- Text material references and compact approval receipts reduce repeated content in the local model context.
- Reviewed task handoffs and reference-only delegation arguments; the local model submits task instructions for review before selecting approved content for cloud collaboration.
- Route-scoped collaboration guidance and approved material references supplied directly in model context.
- Cloud delegation remains discoverable throughout cloud-routed requests; execution enforces material approval.
- Routing history limited to 1,000 Unicode characters across up to three recent user turns.
- Progress, cancellation, recovery, and result delivery through OpenCode sessions.
- Collaboration stages restore from persisted task and review records when a terminal connects or reconnects.
- User cancellation stops the active task and concurrent reviews; subsequent requests start normally.
- Session deletion removes associated review and run records, including deletions made while the plugin was unloaded.
- Recovery reports deleted collaboration sessions.

### Setup and materials

- `/xcospan` model configuration, connection checks, and lifecycle controls.
- Saving unchanged model settings keeps collaboration available and completes immediately.
- Installation, update, and removal through OpenCode plugin commands.
- A materials Skill for task-driven extraction and source verification, with complete readable text export to a new local file.
- Package documentation and diagrams with validated relative links.

### Verification

- Package verification on Linux, macOS, and Windows with Node.js 22 and 24.
- Native Windows terminal tests using ConPTY, OCR data, and special-character workspaces.
- Provider credentials, environment credentials, and account-store authentication coverage.
- A real-model TUI journey covering local execution, text and file collaboration, and return to local execution in one session.
- A live quality check that approves model-generated candidates unchanged and checks privacy boundaries before cloud submission.
- Tarball installation, release validation, and npm publication workflows.
- Commit-history secret scanning and dependency audits in pull-request verification.

```sh

bun run check
bun run test:package
```

## Source setup

To load a source checkout into OpenCode:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --branch main https://github.com/XHToken/opencode-XCoSpan.git
cd opencode-XCoSpan

```

`setup` builds the TUI and registers the checkout in global OpenCode configuration, preserving existing settings and comments. Repeating it keeps a single entry. Report vulnerabilities privately to [tokenspark-security@googlegroups.com](mailto:tokenspark-security@googlegroups.com), identifying this repository and the affected version or commit. ## Data and execution boundaries

Originals, redaction comparisons, candidate revisions, and task associations are stored in local OpenCode plugin storage. These records can contain sensitive data and follow the OpenCode data directory's access and retention policies. Deleting a native conversation removes its associated review, run, and child-index records. Startup reconciles deletions made while XCoSpan was unloaded. Plugin removal retains records for subsequent reinstallation.

The plugin creates cloud sessions with an explicit model, approved task and materials, and scoped public-information tools. Their context excludes parent-session history and baseline workspace instructions. Delegation waits for approval before starting. Review RPC methods are not exposed as model tools.

The model selects materials and writes the delegated task. Redaction quality requires human review. The local model retains original context and can include identifying information when assembling a task. Complete-candidate review covers the objective, related context, materials, and expected output. The user checks, edits, and approves the actual outbound revision. Subsequent cloud requests include the delegated task's execution history and authorized tool results.

Native `webfetch` in a delegated session filters connections to public addresses. Literal IPs, resolved DNS addresses, and redirected connections are checked to block loopback, private, and link-local addresses. The implementation uses `request-filtering-agent` and Got, preserving native permission checks, content handling, and cancellation. `websearch` uses the host-configured search service. The deployment environment must govern that service and network behavior from other plugins or MCP servers.

The plugin controls sessions created through its delegation tool. The host and operating system govern the primary agent's shell, other plugins, MCP services, and external network permissions. Operating-system network isolation requires deployment-level controls.

Local-role capabilities use the configured local model by default. A remote provider receives the corresponding inputs. Optional routing and redaction HTTP services are restricted to loopback and cannot redirect.

User cancellation stops the associated native parent execution and its pending reviews. Cloud cancellation also waits for the native child session to stop. Historical cancelled records do not interrupt a later task. Interrupted runs with uncertain outcomes remain `unknown` for recovery checks. Recovery does not rerun cloud work. Exposing an unauthenticated OpenCode service or its local data directory can expose review RPC methods or sensitive materials; use host authentication and local access controls.

When reporting an issue, provide redacted reproduction steps, the OpenCode version, and relevant errors. Exclude credentials, original private documents, and complete private conversations.

# Architecture

The plugin uses native OpenCode models, sessions, tools, Skills, RPC, and TUI APIs. The local model chooses the work plan. The plugin integrates routing, enforces review, manages delegation, and presents actual execution progress.

```text
OpenCode parent session
  |
  +-- routing -> capabilities -> decision for this request
  |
  +-- local model <-> local tools / Skills
         |
         +-- redact -> review <-> TUI material review
         |
         +-- cloud_delegate -> review <-> TUI outbound approval
                                  |
                               delegate
                                  |
                         isolated OpenCode session
                            context / network
                                  |
                  actual result -> parent tool -> parent session

TUI <-> RPC <-> reviews / run records / configuration
TUI <-- native session and tool events
```

## Module responsibilities

| Module                                  | Responsibility                                                       |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/index.ts`                          | Register agents, tools, Skills, and RPC; compose modules             |
| `src/routing.ts`, `src/capabilities.ts` | Per-request routing, model generation, and local capability services |
| `src/redact.ts`, `src/review.ts`        | Redaction tools, candidate revisions, and human review               |
| `src/delegate.ts`                       | Cloud sessions, cancellation, recovery, and result delivery          |
| `src/context.ts`, `src/network.ts`      | Approved context and cloud-tool network boundaries                   |
| `src/management.ts`, `src/settings*.ts` | Model configuration, JSONC edits, lifecycle, and removal             |
| `src/rpc.ts`, `src/types.ts`            | Communication and persistent data contracts                          |
| `src/tui/`, `src/status.ts`             | Setup, review, real execution events, and usage                      |
| `skills/materials/`                     | Task-driven local materials and unified format extraction            |

## Model guidance

`src/prompts.ts` defines the coordinator and cloud worker's system instructions. They describe outcomes, material sufficiency, review continuity, delegation requirements, and evidence-based completion. The model chooses its tools and working sequence from the task and available capabilities. The routing hook adds the current query's decision. Collaboration preparation guidance is injected for cloud-routed requests. After material approval, the context hook supplies the current review ID and the ID-only delegation contract. Relevant Skills provide on-demand operational guidance. Tool execution and persistent state enforce approval, permissions, cancellation, and delivery.

## Execution invariants

- Routing is associated with the user message ID. Tool rounds within one request reuse its decision. Inputs include the current tool descriptions, discovered Skills, and configured model roles. The current query is sent in full. Routing history contains up to three prior user turns, each with the user text and last assistant text, sharing a total budget of 1,000 Unicode characters. Selection prioritizes the latest turn with at most 500 characters per entry, retains chronological order, and marks truncated entries. Historical reasoning and tool payloads are excluded. The parent agent retains its full native context.
- Routing receives the local execution tool catalog; cloud delegation is excluded from local capability assessment.
- Tool registration follows configured capabilities. Image redaction is exposed when a local redaction service is configured; routing reads the resulting tool set.
- The materials Skill defines selection and verification guidance. A small helper delegates format detection and extraction to Xberg's registry, retaining source hashes, pages, tables, and warnings. Its optional `--text-output` writes complete extracted text with readable line breaks to a new local file. The model chooses when to use extraction, OCR, spreadsheet calculation, or visual inspection.
- The model sees `cloud_delegate` throughout a cloud-routed request, including preparation. Its arguments reference approved materials. Execution checks the route, review ownership, and approval state before creating an outbound candidate; incomplete or failed review prevents delegation.
- Prepared text files can be referenced by `redact.files`; native read and external-directory permissions apply. Full source text and approved text stay in review storage instead of being copied into tool arguments and approval results.
- The model prepares task instructions and evidence through material review. `cloud_delegate` accepts only approved review IDs; the plugin uses the first reviewed text as task instructions and attaches the remaining reviewed materials. Final confirmation displays the complete candidate and supports user edits.
- Approval binds the session, tool call, and candidate revision. Cloud delegation receives approved content.
- Tool inputs, results, and persistent records remain associated. Recovery does not rerun completed work.
- Cancellation propagates through the parent session, tool, cloud session, and model request.
- UI state comes from actual events and persistent facts. The model determines the sequence of task actions.

## Package boundary

Root-level `server.ts`, `tui.tsx`, and `rpc.ts` are thin entrypoints required by OpenCode's local directory discovery protocol. They connect the server module, compiled TUI, and RPC contract. Package exports use the same implementation. OpenCode loads server-side TypeScript; `src/tui/` is compiled to `dist/tui.js`, with OpenTUI and Solid supplied by the host's shared runtime.

Follow [Installation](../README.md#installation) to install the npm package through `opencode plugin add @iflytekopensource/opencode-xcospan`, then use the [Quick start](../README.md#quick-start) to configure model roles through `/xcospan`. Developers can follow [Source setup](../CONTRIBUTING.md#source-setup); `bun run setup` builds and registers the checkout in OpenCode's global configuration. Setup and lifecycle controls use the host's configuration sources; the [installation guide](../README.md#update-or-uninstall) covers updates and removal for each source.

The package allowlist includes server source, compiled TUI, the shipped Skill, and essential package documentation. Tests, fixtures, build scripts, and local records stay in the development checkout. `test:package` checks the tarball, tests native package commands against an isolated registry, installs it with npm and Bun, and runs real host integration tests. The materials helper runs through Bun on PATH; host-loaded plugin code uses OpenCode's runtime.

API references: [OpenCode V2 plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins), [TUI extensions](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/cli).

# Compatibility

## Host and operating systems

XCoSpan targets OpenCode 2.0.27. The package verification workflow is configured for Node.js 22 and 24 on Linux, macOS, and native Windows x64 (Windows Server 2025). It installs the actual tarball with npm and Bun, loads it into OpenCode, and exercises native terminal setup, review, cancellation, recovery, and removal. Test workspaces and materials include spaces, non-ASCII characters, and URL-reserved characters.

The bundled material helper uses Bun 1.4.3 and Xberg 1.3.10. Xberg distributes a native Windows x64 binary. The published Xberg 1.3.10 packages do not include macOS Intel (x64) or Windows ARM64 binaries. The bundled extraction helper cannot run natively on those architectures. Use an available local extraction tool through the model's tools and Skills.

Per-platform validation results are recorded in the verification workflow job logs. The Linux Node.js 24 job also uploads the verified package and checksum.

### Windows quick start

Use Windows Terminal with PowerShell. Install the plugin with the command from [Installation](../README.md#installation):

```powershell
opencode plugin add @iflytekopensource/opencode-xcospan
```

For development checkouts, follow [Source setup](../CONTRIBUTING.md#source-setup).

Open your workspace in OpenCode, then enter `/xcospan` to choose accounts and models, test the connection, and start. Keep Bun on the PATH inherited by OpenCode when using the material helper. Install Bun using its [official Windows instructions](https://bun.com/docs/installation), then reopen the terminal and OpenCode.

Quote file paths containing spaces. The helper accepts native drive paths and resolves them through the operating system. It keeps the original file unchanged.

For OCR, install the required language files from [Tesseract's data repository](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tessdata_fast), and set `TESSDATA_PREFIX` to the directory containing those files before starting OpenCode. For example, if English data is already installed there:

```powershell
$env:TESSDATA_PREFIX = "C:\Tools\tessdata"
opencode
```

Model credentials supplied through environment variables must also reach the OpenCode service process. Account connections through `/connect` use OpenCode's credential store.

### Terminal behavior

Automated Windows tests use Bun's native ConPTY support. XCoSpan review controls have keyboard shortcuts, including editing, saving, approval, cancellation, and image navigation. Bun documents mouse-tracking limitations on older Windows ConPTY versions; see [platform differences](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/child-process#platform-differences). Windows 11 with Windows Terminal is recommended for interactive use.

## Provider protocols and authentication

The local and cloud roles are independent OpenCode model references. Protocol and authentication handling belongs to the selected native provider package.

| API              | Custom provider selection | Native package                             |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Chat Completions | OpenAI Chat Completions   | `@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible` |
| Responses        | OpenAI Responses          | `@opencode/ai/providers/openai`            |
| Messages         | Anthropic Messages        | `@opencode/ai/providers/anthropic`         |

Use the endpoint's base address, excluding `/chat/completions` or `/responses`. Use the provider's published model limits. The connection test invokes a tool and reads its result through the actual host.

Native integration tests verify explicit provider credentials, environment credentials, and account-store credentials. They also verify authentication failure and correction. Provider-specific OAuth refresh, command credentials, WebSocket transports, and individual model services require dedicated validation.

Live runs accept arbitrary provider definitions through the [live configuration](../test/README.md#live-model-configuration). Run the same journey for each protocol and role pairing to verify routing, redaction, user review, real delegation, and return to local execution. Validation checks the completed response stream, including `response.failed` events that can follow HTTP 200.

Tool selection follows the provider's requirements for the selected reasoning mode. OpenCode's model loop lets the model choose tools, and provider errors are displayed to the user.

# Configuration and capability services

## Models and scope

Follow [Installation](../README.md#installation), then enter `/xcospan` in OpenCode and choose **Configure models** to select the local-role and cloud models. The interface reads OpenCode's model catalog, supports account connections and custom services, and can check each model's connection and tool-calling support. Checks incur actual provider usage and can be cancelled.

Settings are saved to the selected OpenCode JSON / JSONC source, preserving unrelated values and comments. Concurrent changes require a reload. Stop active tasks before changing models. Saving preserves the current default agent; users can explicitly choose XCoSpan as the default for new sessions.

Plugin options for manual configuration:

| Field                          | Meaning                                                                                |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `localModel`                   | Required `{ providerID, id }` reference for the local role                             |
| `cloudModel`                   | Required `{ providerID, id }` reference for cloud collaboration                        |
| `enabled`                      | Optional; `false` disables collaboration while keeping management available            |
| `routeURL`                     | Optional local routing service URL                                                     |
| `redactURL`                    | Optional local redaction service URL; required for image redaction                     |
| `routeKeyEnv` / `redactKeyEnv` | Optional environment variable names containing service Bearer credentials              |
| `timeoutMs`                    | Optional positive integer timeout in milliseconds for routing and redaction HTTP calls |

The management interface saves `previousDefaultAgent` to restore the previous default.

OpenCode provider configuration controls API addresses, protocols, accounts, tool capabilities, context windows, and output limits. Model choices come from configuration. Environment variables must reach the OpenCode service that makes requests; see the [provider environment documentation](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/providers#environment).

## Material tools

The bundled `xcospan-materials` Skill runs its extraction helper with Bun. Keep Bun 1.4.3 on the OpenCode process's PATH. The npm package includes the helper and its Xberg dependency. OCR additionally requires local Tesseract language data for the languages selected by the task; exact spreadsheet calculations require an available spreadsheet-capable tool. These tool dependencies are separate from model account configuration.

## Routing

Each new query is routed before the local model's first call. Subsequent tool rounds reuse that decision. Routing uses the selected local-role model by default, or `routeURL` when configured.

```text
POST routeURL
{
  query: string,
  context: SessionMessageInfo[],
  files: SessionMessageUser["files"],
  capabilities: {
    localModel: { providerID: string, id: string },
    cloudModel: { providerID: string, id: string },
    tools: { name: string, description: string }[],
    skills: { name: string, description?: string }[]
  }
}
-> { reason: string, route: 0 | 1 }
```

`context` contains native session messages preceding the current query. `files` contains the current user message's native attachment descriptions. Their fields follow the supported OpenCode SDK types. `capabilities` is collected from the current host tool set, Skill discovery, and configured model roles; routing evaluates the task against that available setup.

`route=0` selects local execution; `route=1` selects cloud collaboration. The plugin maps this strict algorithm result to its internal `cloud` flag for session state and execution. The local model selects materials, preparation steps, and delegation content from the task and context.

## Redaction

Text redaction uses the selected local-role model by default. The local model uses the `xcospan-materials` Skill and suitable local tools to select and extract the content needed for the task before redaction. When `redactURL` is configured, that service handles text and images and the plugin registers `redact_image`. Available tools and routing inputs reflect this configuration.

```text
POST redactURL
{ content: Content }
-> { content: Content, changes: string }

Content =
  { type: "text", text: string }
  | { type: "image", mime: "image/png" | "image/jpeg" | "image/webp", data: string }
```

Image `data` contains the complete base64-encoded bytes. Output preserves the input content type. `changes` describes the transformation. The user reviews service output before it can be delegated.

Both service URLs must use loopback addresses; redirects are rejected. Errors surface directly, and cancellation reaches the request. Originals, candidates, change descriptions, and approved revisions are stored in OpenCode plugin storage.

## Built-in algorithm policy

Routing evaluates the current query and session context against the configured model and available tools. The decision considers the complete deliverable, required reasoning, and a verification path. Model identity, file format, domain, and task length are assessed within those requirements. Invalid JSON or an invalid decision stops the request.

Text redaction covers direct and indirect identifiers, credentials, business entities, financial and contractual data, and identifying combinations. This policy includes contract amounts, payment percentages, and liability percentages. Every candidate is shown against its original; users can edit the candidate to retain facts needed for the delegated task. The local agent uses the reviewed version when preparing the final outbound task.

Built-in text redaction sends the input to the configured local-role model and returns a complete text candidate. The sensitive-data categories follow Privacy Gateway's `string_only` policy at revision `6256c66fb869b40959d75cbfa29a3d4864294228`. External redaction engines integrate through the HTTP service contract above.

Users review each model-generated candidate for sensitive-data coverage, document structure, and placeholder consistency. The original and approved candidate remain in plugin storage for comparison. The plugin requires material review and approval of the complete outbound task before cloud execution.

## Review and outbound content

`redact` accepts a task handoff in `content` and optional `files` containing selected UTF-8 text. File reads use native read permissions before loading the complete local text; source paths stay local. The tool returns a compact approval receipt. `redact` / `redact_image` return the approved material's review ID. `cloud_delegate` accepts `reviewIds`: the reviewed text handoff first, then approved supporting materials. The handoff contains the objective, relevant context, constraints, and requested output. The plugin assembles these approved contents into the complete candidate for final editing and confirmation. New model-authored instructions require a new material review.

Each save creates a new revision. Approval of the complete candidate starts the cloud task. Failure, rejection, or cancellation stops the pending send. Subsequent cloud requests include the approved task, its own execution history, and authorized tool results.

## Disable, remove, and recover

- Use `/xcospan` to stop the current task, return to the previous agent, or disable / enable collaboration.
- Removal acts on the selected configuration source. Check `/plugins` for other loading sources.
- After host interruption, reviews with a lost caller become `interrupted`. Runs whose outcome cannot be confirmed become `unknown`.
- Persistent associations recover delivery of completed cloud results. Repeated recovery is idempotent.

See [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md) for data-access and deployment boundaries.

## Routing conversation context

Each new user query receives its own routing decision. Tool rounds within that query reuse the decision. The router receives the complete current query and up to three recent user turns, with the user text and last assistant text from each turn. Historical text shares a total budget of 1,000 Unicode characters. The latest turn is selected first, with at most 500 characters per entry; remaining space holds older context. Entries retain chronological order and a `truncated` flag. This budget applies to historical text; the current query, routing instructions, and capability descriptions are separate. Historical tool output and reasoning are omitted. Current attachments and the available capability descriptions accompany the query. The parent agent keeps its full native context.

# Releasing

## Repository configuration

- Align `LICENSE`, the package license identifier, README badges, and contribution terms with the [XHToken community license](https://github.com/XHToken/community/blob/main/LICENSE). Preserve contributor attribution and third-party notices. Verify community, conduct, and security contacts against the [community policies](https://github.com/XHToken/community#governance--policies).
- Set `main` as the default branch. Pull requests target `main`; Check validates pushes and pull requests for that branch.
- Configure `NPM_TOKEN` as a repository secret or an `npm` environment secret, using a granular token with publication rights to the package scope. Publication checks for this secret before the verification matrix. Validation runs with `publish=false` do not require publication credentials.
- Configure the `live-tests` environment with `XCOSPAN_LIVE_CONFIG` using the schema in [Testing](../test/README.md#live-model-configuration). Live models checks for this secret before installing dependencies.
- Apply the desired environment approval rules. A publication can require approval for both its credential check and its publishing job.
- Protect `main` against force pushes and deletion, and require the Check jobs before merging. Branch protection and environment controls depend on repository permissions and the GitHub plan.
- Check the repository's Actions page after changes to branches or workflow settings. Verify the intended triggers and results before publishing a version.

## Pipeline

```text
Pull request / main
  -> workflow and shell validation
  -> commit-history secret scan and dependency audit
  -> Linux + macOS + Windows, Node 22 + 24
  -> types, formatting, unit tests
  -> build and inspect npm tarball
  -> native plugin add / check / update / remove against the tarball registry
  -> clean npm install -> native host and TUI tests
  -> clean Bun install -> exports and native extraction
  -> npm publish --dry-run
  -> verified tarball + SHA-256 artifact

Version tag on main
  -> exact version and source validation
  -> the same verification pipeline
  -> verify artifact checksum -> publish that tarball with NPM_TOKEN
  -> GitHub release with the published tarball and checksum
```

Build and host versions come from `package.json`. Actions are pinned to commit SHAs. Runtime package tests install from the tarball in temporary consumer directories. Publish jobs use the verified tarball and checksum produced by the verification job.

## Validate a release

Run the Release workflow manually on a branch, leaving `publish` disabled:

```sh
gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f publish=false
```

With `publish=false`, the workflow runs version checks, platform verification, artifact transfer, checksum verification, and `npm publish --dry-run`. Registry upload requires `publish=true` and publication credentials.

For local artifact verification:

```sh
bun run check
bun run test:package --output dist/release
bun run test:package --artifact /absolute/path/to/package.tgz
```

Download the `npm-package` artifact from a successful workflow to inspect the exact candidate.

## npm credentials

The package name and `publishConfig` in `package.json` define the destination. Confirm the signed-in account has publish rights to its scope with `npm whoami` and npm's package or organization settings.

The release workflow reads `NPM_TOKEN` from GitHub Actions secrets. Configure a granular token with publish access to `@iflytekopensource` and Bypass 2FA enabled. Store the token in the secret manager, track its expiry, and rotate it before expiration. npm limits write tokens to 90 days. Use a prerelease version and an explicit `next` or `test` dist-tag during testing.

## Trusted publishing configuration

npm is retiring direct publication with bypass-2FA tokens in January 2027. To migrate the release workflow to OIDC, configure the package's trusted publisher:

| Field             | Value                                |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| GitHub owner      | `XHToken`                            |
| Repository        | `opencode-XCoSpan`                   |
| Workflow filename | `release.yml`                        |
| Environment       | `npm`                                |
| Allowed action    | Direct publishing with `npm publish` |

The GitHub `npm` environment can require maintainer review. For the OIDC migration, grant the publishing job `id-token: write`, remove `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, and retain npm 12.2.0 or later. Ensure the package's repository URL matches the publishing repository. Verify an actual publication before retiring the token.

New trusted-publisher configurations must complete their first successful publication within 48 hours. npm generates provenance for public packages from public repositories; private repositories do not produce that provenance. Maintainers manage repository visibility in GitHub settings.

## Publish a version

1. Update `package.json`, `bun.lock`, and `CHANGELOG.md` together. Describe user-visible changes and breaking contracts. Documentation and diagrams use relative links and ship in the package; artifact validation checks their targets. Verify README rendering on GitHub and npm after publication.
2. Merge the reviewed revision into `main` and inspect its CI result.
3. Push a tag matching the exact version, such as `v0.1.0` or `v0.2.0-rc.1`. The Release workflow rejects version mismatches and commits outside `main`.
4. Approve the GitHub environment if configured. Stable versions publish to `latest`; prereleases publish to `next`.
5. Verify the registry version, dist-tag, and integrity, then run the README's unversioned `opencode plugin add @iflytekopensource/opencode-xcospan` command in a clean OpenCode environment. Confirm existing model accounts, `/xcospan` setup, update and removal. Run the [real-model quick-start journey](../test/README.md#live-model-configuration) with `XCOSPAN_INSTALL_SPEC` set to the published package to verify registry installation through delivery.

For a manual publish, select the existing version tag and enable `publish`. Manual branch runs perform release validation. Publication requires a version tag.

Publishing failures fail the workflow. If npm accepted a version but GitHub release creation failed, rerun only the failed job; do not republish that version. npm versions are immutable.

## Temporary registry tests

Use a unique prerelease version with an explicit `test` dist-tag. Publish the verified tarball, download that exact version from npm, compare its integrity, and run `test:package --artifact` against the downloaded file.

Remove only the test version with `npm unpublish <name>@<test-version>`. Verify that the version and its dist-tag are no longer available. Unpublishing the last version may require `--force` and prevents new publications under that package name for 24 hours; the removed version can never be reused. Plan tests around that registry constraint.

## Other workflows

- **Live models:** explicit manual run with the `live-tests` environment's `XCOSPAN_LIVE_CONFIG` secret. Supply the JSON schema in [Testing](../test/README.md), with credentials resolved in provider settings. The runner deletes configuration and request diagnostics after the run. Paid model tests never run for pull requests.
- **Dependency audit:** every verification run, plus weekly and manually triggered `bun audit`.
- **Dependabot:** automatic version-update pull requests are paused for Bun and GitHub Actions (`open-pull-requests-limit: 0`). Security-update settings remain unchanged. Maintainers review dependency upgrades alongside the verification checks.
